chunks: Laith al-Muradi asked him (peace be upon him): About a man who comes to Mecca during the days of Mina after finishing the visitation of the House, so he performs Tawaf around the House voluntarily, then he said:
"Staying in Mina is more beloved to me."

key_terms.الْمُقَامُ: Staying/residing, referring to remaining in a specific location.
key_terms.تَطَوُّعاً: Voluntarily, referring to a non-obligatory act of worship.
key_terms.زِيَارَةِ الْبَيْتِ: Visitation of the House (Kaaba), referring to the initial Tawaf or Umrah.
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a valley and camp area near Mecca, central to Hajj rituals.

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred location for a pilgrim performing voluntary Tawaf during the days of Mina?
ai.summary: Laith al-Muradi asked Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about the preferred location for a pilgrim who arrives in Mecca during the days of Mina after completing the initial visitation of the Kaaba and wishes to perform a voluntary Tawaf. The Imam replied that staying in Mina is more beloved to him, indicating the preference for remaining in the Mina camp during the days of Tashriq rather than returning to Mecca for additional times to Mecca for voluntary rituals. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on adhering to the specific temporal and spatial rituals of Hajj, where the merit of Mina during the days of Tashriq outweighs the convenience of performing extra Tawaf in Mecca, reflecting the principle of *ibtida'* (initiation) in ritual timing.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3014 - Laith Al-Muradi asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who goes to Mecca during the days of Mina after completing the visitation of the House and performs Tawaf around the Kaaba voluntarily.
Imam (as) replied: "Staying in Mina is more beloved to me."
